compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The sibling index story builds a ranked similar-ticket query API but surfaces nothing. This story carries its results to users on every surface that creates a ticket.

Today `rebar create` warns only when a new title normalizes byte-identically to a recent one: `duplicate_create_warning` (`src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:117-119`), gated by `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` (`:129`), matching on `title_norm` equality (`:103`). ADR 0122 measured that stratum at 1,431 of 1,524 recorded duplicate pairs. The remaining 93 differ in wording and are invisible to equality matching; they are why agents re-file work that already has a ticket.

## Approach

### The advisory seam, and why a per-site fix is the wrong one

The create result already carries `duplicate_warning` and `description_warning`, and the seam spans more sites than `create`. `_lib_writes.py` builds its return dicts by hand-copying named advisory keys — `duplicate_warning` at `:172` and `:179` for create, and again at `:224` and `:231` for idea, each alongside a `description_warning` line. `_commands/composer.py:466-467` re-emits both on CLI stderr so stdout stays pure in either output mode; `_commands/idea.py:92-93` does the same for `rebar idea`.

Because every one of those sites names its keys individually, an advisory key added only to `create` is silently dropped from `idea()`'s return dict and never reaches the idea CLI. Adding one more hand-copied key would work today and reproduce the same gap for the next advisory.

Advisory pass-through is therefore made generic at the `create_core` boundary, so advisory keys propagate without a per-site edit. `idea` is covered by criteria of its own, because generic propagation is the claim most worth testing directly rather than inferring.

`src/rebar/schemas/create_result.schema.json` already documents the advisory contract and is extended with `similar_tickets`, including `score`'s range and direction — the index story normalizes `score` to the closed interval 0 to 1, 1 most relevant, and a consumer cannot assert on it without that documented.

### Query construction

The advisory is computed after the write succeeds, so a retrieval failure can never fail a completed create — the same disposition the existing probe has at `recent_creates.py:151`, where a bare `except Exception` returns `None` under the comment "an advisory notice must never fail a completed write".

The query passes the just-created ticket's own id for exclusion, because catch-up will already have indexed it and it would otherwise rank as its own top match. The existing probe already establishes this shape: its journal scan filters `e["id"] != ticket_id` at `:101`, so a create does not match itself.

Every failure path yields an empty `similar_tickets` field and leaves the exit status unchanged. The index story owns the diagnostic logging; this story asserts the create's disposition.

### Gating

The gate is `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`, the key that already gates create-time duplicate advice. This is that same advice with ranked results, so a second key would split one user-facing behaviour across two switches. No new config key is added.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar create --output json` returns a `similar_tickets` array. Checked by: a CLI test asserting the field is present.
- [ ] The library `create_ticket` return dict carries `similar_tickets`. Checked by: a library test asserting the key is present.
- [ ] MCP `create_ticket` output carries `similar_tickets`. Checked by: an MCP test asserting the key is present in the tool result.
- [ ] The library `idea()` return dict carries `similar_tickets`. Checked by: a library test asserting the key is present on an idea create.
- [ ] The `rebar idea` CLI surfaces `similar_tickets` on stderr. Checked by: a CLI test capturing stderr on an idea create.
- [ ] `rebar create` surfaces `similar_tickets` on stderr in text output mode. Checked by: a CLI test capturing stderr.
- [ ] Advisory keys propagate from `create_core` without a per-key edit at the `_lib_writes.py` and `idea` sites. Checked by: a test adding a synthetic advisory key at the `create_core` boundary and asserting it reaches both the create and idea return dicts.
- [ ] `create_result.schema.json` documents `similar_tickets` including `score`'s range and direction. Checked by: a schema test validating a sample result against the committed schema.
- [ ] A created ticket's own id never appears in its own `similar_tickets` results. Checked by: a test creating a ticket whose text matches itself strongly and asserting its id is absent.
- [ ] A create exits 0 with an empty `similar_tickets` when retrieval returns empty. Checked by: a test injecting an empty retrieval and asserting exit status and field contents.
- [ ] A create exits 0 with an empty `similar_tickets` when retrieval raises. Checked by: a test injecting a raising retrieval and asserting exit status and field contents.
- [ ] A create's ticket is written and readable when retrieval raises. Checked by: the same test reading the ticket afterwards.
- [ ] `similar_tickets` is empty when `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` is false. Checked by: a test with the key disabled.
- [ ] No new configuration key is introduced. Checked by: `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exiting 0.
- [ ] Every module added or modified under `src/rebar/` is at most 800 lines. Checked by: the CI module-size gate.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0. Checked by: running it.

file_impact.reason: Replace hand-copied advisory keys at the create and idea return sites with generic pass-through
Emit similar_tickets on CLI stderr alongside the existing advisories
Carry advisories generically instead of re-emitting them key by key
Compute the ranked advisory after the write, under the existing config gate
Document similar_tickets including the score range and direction

compiled_state.title: Surface ranked similar tickets on every create and idea surface
